subject: Service discovery contract & intermediate CA allocation
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.example.com>

Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.example.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.example.com
Date: 2026-09-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Service discovery contract & intermediate CA allocation

Hi team,

Thanks again for the call this morning. As discussed, I'm attaching an initial draft of a lightweight "service discovery contract" that captures roles and responsibilities for private FQDN ownership, intermediate CA allocation, and TLS termination patterns for the VPC-hosted Redwood Private deployment. The goal is to lock the operational contract so we can provision FQDNs and issue intermediate certs without re-running security approvals.

High level asks in the draft:
- Acme SRE to indicate which teams will own each private zone and who will accept CSR proofs.
- Agreement on where intermediate CA private keys are stored (customer KMS vs. Redwood-managed HSM).
- Rotation cadence (we propose quarterly for intermediates, 30-day overlap for rollover).
- Default TLS termination model: mutual TLS at client side, optional TLS termination at Redwoods' private endpoint with strict pinning if requested.

Please review the attached "service-discovery-contract-v1.pdf" and call out anything that would block procurement or security sign-off. Laura / Karthik — can you take first pass on the CSR flow and the KMS recommendations?

Next steps: if everyone is aligned by EOD Thursday we'll schedule a short working call to sign the DocuSign and kick off CSR exchanges.

Thanks,
Jordan
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
[jordan.blake@redwood.example.com]

Attachment: service-discovery-contract-v1.pdf (application/pdf, 245 KB)

From: SRE Team <sre-team@acme-corp.com>

Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.example.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.example.com
Date: 2026-09-22T10:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Service discovery contract & intermediate CA allocation

Jordan,

Appreciate the doc — this is a good starting point. A few clarifying questions from Acme SRE: 

1) Intermediate CA custody: our security team prefers customer KMS (cloud KMS backed by HSM). Is Redwood able to accept signed intermediates rather than storing keys? We need an option where Acme generates the intermediate and provides the cert chain (so private key never leaves our KMS).

2) Rotation/rollback: the proposal for quarterly rotation is OK, but we need a documented rollback window and automated canary validation. Can you include a simple health-check plan for cert swaps?

3) Service discovery: we operate three private zones (prod.us.acme, staging.us.acme, dev.us.acme). We need explicit mapping in the contract listing which teams own which zones and the contact for CSR approvals.

Also, our security team asked whether Redwood supports short-lived server certs (hours) issued via an ACME-like flow if we push keys into an HSM. That would help reduce blast radius.

We can respond in-line in the PDF, or you can update and push a new version — whichever is easier.

Thanks,
Priya (on behalf of Acme SRE)
sre-team@acme-corp.com

Thanks Priya — good questions. A few notes from the ops/security side (high level):

- Custody model: we can accept signed intermediate certs from customer KMS and run Redwood's serving fleet with the provided chain — this avoids storing the private key on our side. We'll document the CSR/CSR-signer workflow in the contract.

- Short-lived certs: Redwood runtime supports short-lived server cert rotation; however an ACME-like flow will require a secure CSR callback endpoint from Acme (or an out-of-band CSR pull). If Acme wants keys fully inside HSM and rotation automated, we'll need to agree on a signed webhook or SFTP-based CSR handoff (we include a csr-template-intermediate.pem that you can use to generate the request).

- Rotation/rollback plan: propose the following minimal health checks for cert swap (we'll add to the contract):
  * Canary traffic to 1-2 endpoints with expected latency bounds.
  * KV cache validation for active sessions (to detect edge failures).
  * Automated fallback for 10 minutes to previous cert if error rate > 1%.

- Zone mapping: please confirm the explicit list (prod, staging, dev). We'll add a table and contact email per zone.

I've attached a CSR template (csr-template-intermediate.pem) and a short matrix for the CSR signer roles. If Acme wants us to host the intermediate key we can provide HSM-backed storage, but we recommend customer KMS for regulated workloads.

Laura Bennett
Principal Product Manager, Platform Security | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.example.com

Attachments: csr-template-intermediate.pem (text/plain, 2 KB)

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.example.com>

Date: 2026-09-22T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Service discovery contract & intermediate CA allocation

Adding infra/runbook perspective and a proposed schedule.

- Termination patterns: for private endpoints we recommend a default of mTLS between client and Redwood edge with optional TLS re-termination inside Redwood only when explicit auditing is in place. Pattern options:
  1) End-to-end mTLS (client cert -> Redwood service): highest security, no re-termination.
  2) mTLS to edge, short-lived server certs to service (rotate hourly/daily).
  3) Edge termination + downstream TLS with pinned intermediate (only for performance-sensitive endpoints).

- Rotation schedule: attached is a small spreadsheet with the proposed rollout: staggered per region, intermediates rotate quarterly, server short-lived certs rotate daily for staging and hourly for dev canaries. We included overlap windows (30 days) and backout steps.

- Automation hooks: we'll add probe endpoints that validate the new chain before flipping global traffic. A basic plan: deploy cert to canary -> run 3x synthetic checks -> promote if green -> monitor for 60 minutes; rollback automatically if error budget exceeded.

Quote from Priya that I want to acknowledge: "short-lived server certs (hours) issued via an ACME-like flow" — we can support that but will need either (a) Acme-run ACME server with webhook to accept CSRs or (b) Redwood-operated short-lived issuer that signs ephemeral certs upon API request gated by mutual auth. Both require design work; recommend we scope MVP with option (b) under a restricted SLA.

Attachment: rotation-proposal-2026Q4.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, 18 KB)

Thanks everyone — good alignment. Quick summary and action items so we can move to sign-off: 

1) Custody: Acme will generate intermediates in your KMS and provide signed intermediate certs to Redwood (no private key transfer). Action: Acme SRE to confirm the KMS key policy and provide an endpoint for CSR verification by Wed 2026-09-29.

2) CSR flow: Laura to produce a documented CSR pull/push flow and a filled template. Action: Laura to upload v1.1 of the contract with the CSR appendix (I'll review).

3) Short-lived certs: Redwood will scope an MVP for an Redwood-issued short-lived cert service (option b from Mina). Action: Karthik and Mina to produce a 1-page solution brief and estimate by 2026-10-06.

4) Rotation/rollback: agreed on quarterly intermediate rotation with 30-day overlap and the canary health checks Mina described. Action: Acme to confirm zone contact list; Jordan will create the DocuSign envelope once the updated PDF is posted.

I've uploaded an updated contract draft with the CSR appendix: service-discovery-contract-v1.1.pdf and started a DocuSign envelope (link above). Let's aim to have signatures by 10/05 so infra provisioning can begin the week after.

If no objections I'll set up a 30-minute working session for Thursday 09/30 at 10:00 AM PT — will send calendar invite.
